summary: Created a local CA named "OS Comparison Root CA" (RSA 4096, self-signed, CA:TRUE, CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison) on node1 (RHEL 7.9), installed it into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and ran update-ca-trust extract, confirmed it's trusted via trust list and openssl verify, and proved end-to-end trust by signing and verifying a leaf certificate. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id, issued a native shutdown -r now reboot with a returned acknowledgement, polled until exec access returned, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified the CA trust state persisted post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 7.9) and confirmed openssl/update-ca-trust availability
Generated 4096-bit RSA CA key and self-signed X.509 CA certificate (CN=OS Comparison Root CA) under /etc/pki/CA/os-comparison-root-ca
Verified certificate is self-signed with CA:TRUE basic constraint
Copied CA cert into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and ran update-ca-trust extract
Verified CA appears in system trust store via trust list and openssl verify against system CA bundle
Issued and verified a test leaf certificate signed by the new CA to prove end-to-end trust chain
Cleaned up temporary leaf cert/key/csr files
Issued backgrounded shutdown -r now on node1, receiving acknowledgement before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned, confirming a new boot_id and new uptime start time
Re-verified CA trust store state (trust list, anchor file, openssl verify) post-restart

evidence.requirement: CA generated on node1 named 'OS Comparison Root CA', self-signed CA:TRUE
evidence.summary: openssl genrsa + req created the CA key/cert; x509 -text output shows Subject=Issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison and Basic Constraints CA:TRUE, confirming a valid self-signed root CA.

evidence.requirement: CA certificate installed as a trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: Copied cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and ran update-ca-trust extract; trust list shows the 'OS Comparison Root CA' label as a trusted certificate and openssl verify against the system ca-bundle.crt returns OK.

evidence.requirement: End-to-end proof the trust store actually honors the new CA
evidence.summary: Signed a test leaf certificate (CN=test.oscomparison.local) with the new CA and verified it against the system CA bundle; verification succeeded, proving real trust chain validation.
Captured boot_id (2fc81aed-3ce8-4a35-8f4c-b73206afa45f) and uptime start prior to reboot, alongside the already-verified healthy CA trust state (cmd-64c60eb8611c4875, cmd-b81cb513678d4b3a).

Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via nohup; command returned REBOOT_ACK immediately, confirmed by the subsequent poll hitting a connection timeout (cmd-ed2eceb86adb4edb), proving the node went down after acknowledging.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving a real restart occurred
evidence.summary: First poll timed out (node down mid-reboot); second poll succeeded with boot_id 5019b2cf-a284-44c6-b89f-0a769741f070 (different from baseline 2fc81aed...) and a new uptime start of 2026-09-03 09:23:44, proving a genuine reboot.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of the CA trust configuration on node1
evidence.summary: After the reboot, trust list still shows 'OS Comparison Root CA', the anchor file is intact, and openssl verify against the system CA bundle still returns OK, confirming persistence across restart.
